title: Man linked to Pickton killed by cops
article: A man linked by evidence to the Robert Pickton farm was shot dead by three police officers in a posh Ontario neighbourhood.

Steve Remian, 38, had exited a car at a park in Oakville when police opened fire at 2:30 a.m. Saturday. Officers had followed his vehicle after receiving a report of a man, possibly armed, behaving strangely at a Tim Hortons.
A rifle was recovered at the shooting scene.

Remian had just used the social-networking website Facebook to reconnect with Mike Clifford of North Vancouver, a high-school friend from their youth in Oakville. Remian's violent death left Clifford in shock.
"Steve wasn't that kind of guy," Clifford said. "It was not like him to be confrontational in any way."
Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, a civilian agency that investigates deaths, sexual assaults and serious injuries connected to police incidents, is probing Remian's death.
"The man got out of the car and was involved in a confrontation with the officers," said Rose Bliss, spokeswoman for the agency.
Clifford remembered Remian as "always a very kind, considerate, sweet guy."
Remian recently mentioned finding a new job in Ontario, repairing vehicles, Clifford said.
Remian's name surfaced in the Pickton trial in March.

A luggage tag bearing his name, and a south Burnaby address, was found on a suitcase in the workshop where the heads, hands and feet of Andrea Joesbury and Sereena Abotsway were found in buckets in a freezer. A hair DNA linked to a Steve Remian turned up on a Hudson's Bay blanket in a dilapidated motorhome where the prosecution alleges a bloody attack took place.

DNA from victim Mona Wilson was found in 15 areas on the blanket, along with a hair from Pickton. Jurors in the trial have heard that DNA can be transferred between people and items, so finding a person's DNA in a location doesn't confirm the person was there.
Pickton, 58, is charged with murdering 26 women. He is on trial on the first six charges relating to Wilson, Abotsway, Joesbury, Georgina Papin, Brenda Wolfe and Marnie Frey.
